## Paper

Counterspeculation, Auctions, and Competitive Sealed Tenders

## World

auction_house

## Institution

Second-price / Vickrey auction.

## Agent type

Private-value bidders or learning bidder agents.

## Theoretical benchmark

Truthful bidding is weakly dominant in a private-value second-price auction; efficient allocation should follow truthful reports.

## Learning setup

Repeated private value draws with learned bidding policies compared against truthful bidding.

## Metrics

Revenue, allocative efficiency, bidder surplus, welfare, truthful-bid regret, overbidding/underbidding rates.

## Main result

Under the standard private-value second-price auction setting, truthful bidding is a weakly dominant strategy, and truthful reports support efficient allocation to the highest-value bidder.

## What they prove

The source is used here for the second-price/Vickrey truthfulness benchmark: truthful bidding is weakly dominant under the relevant private-value assumptions. Regret is this repo's diagnostic proxy for deviations from that benchmark, not the paper's own metric.

## What they only simulate

Not applicable for this card's thesis use: it is treated as an auction-theory benchmark, not as simulation evidence.

## What they do NOT test

Repeated-learning bidder dynamics, neural/MARL bidding policies, and this repo's ex-post regret diagnostics are outside the paper's original one-shot theory role.

## What we need to reproduce

Second-price benchmarks must include truthful bidding, allocative efficiency, and regret/IC proxy, not only bidder reward.

## How our project differs

The paper is one-shot auction theory. This repo studies whether learning bidders approach or fail that benchmark over repeated draws.

## Implementation obligations

Truthful bid benchmark; deterministic tie-breaking; payment equals second price subject to reserve; ex-post regret; bid-curve extraction.

## Metrics to compare in our repo

worlds/auction_house/benchmarks.py; outputs/auction_house_full/summary_aggregate.csv; learned bid curves.

## Failure modes to audit

Interpreting revenue without efficiency/regret; no truthful reference; learned bids below benchmark but still called Vickrey behavior.

## Project code comparison

Compare Counterspeculation, Auctions, and Competitive Sealed Tenders to Auction House second_price outputs. The repo is coherent only if second-price learning is judged against truthfulness, efficiency, and regret.
